sourcedFrom: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 (2010)
cleanIntro: The Hawken is a hooked-breech sidelock, and it comes apart completely differently from any inline. There is no breech plug to unscrew for cleaning — the plug stays in the barrel and the barrel comes off the stock by pulling a single wedge pin. This guide is the CAP LOCK Hawken: ignition is a Number 11 percussion cap on a nipple. The flintlock Hawken is the same rifle with a different lock and has its own guide, because the ignition end is where the two diverge.

steps.title: Drop the ramrod down the bore to check for a charge
steps.action: This is the sidelock owner's chamber check and it is a measurement, not a glance. An empty barrel lets the ramrod down far enough that it stands about an inch proud of the muzzle; a charged one stops it short.
steps.caution: Mark your ramrod at the muzzle line for an empty barrel. It turns this check into a glance you can trust.
steps.quote: VERIFY THAT THE RIFLE BARREL IS NOT LOADED BY DROPPING THE RAMROD DOWN THE BORE. THE RAMROD WILL PROTRUDE ABOUT ONE INCH FROM AN UNCHARGED BARREL.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Re-assembly of the T/C Hawken™ — p.41

steps.title: Take the cap off the nipple
steps.action: On the cap lock Hawken the priming is a percussion cap sitting on the nipple. Remove it before anything else — that is what makes the rifle unprimed.
steps.quote: Ensure that the gun is unprimed. Remove the cap from the nipple on the cap lock or open the frizzen and remove any priming powder that may be present from the flint lock.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Unloading a Charge from the Thompson/Center Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — p.34
steps.warn: Never attempt to clean or disassemble a charged or primed muzzleloading firearm.

steps.title: Remove the ramrod
steps.action: Pull the ramrod out of the thimbles under the barrel and set it aside. It has to be clear before the barrel can come up out of the stock.
steps.quote: Remove the ramrod - set it aside.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Disassembly for Cleaning — p.39

steps.title: Pull the wedge pin
steps.action: One wedge pin through the forend holds the barrel down. It is usually a friction fit — tap it partially out from the far side until you can get fingers on it, then draw it the rest of the way. There is only one, and losing it means the rifle does not go back together.
steps.caution: Use a punch smaller than the escutcheon and tap gently. Driving it hard bruises the wood around the escutcheon.
steps.quote: Pull out the wedge pin. It may be necessary to tap it partially out from the other side in order to grasp the pin and pull it the rest of the way out.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Disassembly for Cleaning — p.39

steps.title: Lift the barrel and pull it forward off the hooked breech
steps.action: With the pin out, the barrel lifts at the muzzle end and then comes forward. That forward motion is what unhooks the breech plug from its slot in the tang — the plug never leaves the barrel, which is the whole point of a hooked breech.
steps.aside: This is as far as the manual takes the Hawken. The lock stays in the stock.
steps.quote: Lift the barrel up as shown (Figure 35) and pull it forward away from the lock assembly. Pull the barrel forward, thus pulling the breech plug out of the breech plug slot in the tang.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Disassembly for Cleaning — p.39

steps.title: Run the bore with the supplied jag
steps.action: Jag onto the ramrod, patch soaked in black-powder solvent, worked the length of the bore until the patches come out clean, then dry patches until it is dry.
steps.prose: Black-powder residue is corrosive rather than merely dirty. Fouling also builds shot to shot until a ball will not seat, which is a safety problem as much as an accuracy one.
steps.quote: Use the cleaning jag that was provided with the Hawken™, and a cleaning patch saturated with a bore cleaner like Thompson/Center’s Number 13® Bore Cleaner (Figure 33).
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Field Cleaning — p.37

steps.title: Flush the barrel with hot soapy water
steps.action: With the barrel off the stock you can stand its muzzle in a pan of hot soapy water and pump a wet patch from the breech end. The barrel works as its own pump. This is the step the hooked breech exists to make easy.
steps.caution: Dry the bore completely before oiling. Water left in a black-powder barrel rusts it fast.
steps.quote: Next in the cleaning process; fill a pan with hot soapy water.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Disassembly for Cleaning — p.39

steps.title: Take the nipple out and clear its threads
steps.action: The nipple unscrews from the drum, and the fire channel behind it is where fouling packs hardest. Clean the nipple and the matching threads in the barrel, dry both thoroughly, then put it back.
steps.aside: The manual gives one instruction covering both locks. On your cap lock rifle it is the nipple — the touchhole bushing belongs to the flintlock.
steps.quote: Remove the nipple on the cap lock model (or the touchhole bushing on the flint lock) and clean it and the corresponding threads in the barrel.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Disassembly for Cleaning — p.40

steps.title: Wipe the lock, hammer and trigger area dry
steps.action: Powder residue blows back over the lock every shot. Wipe the hammer/trigger assembly and the receiver area down and dry the parts before any oil goes on.
steps.quote: Thoroughly wipe any powder residue from the hammer/trigger assembly and receiver. Dry the parts thoroughly.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Disassembly for Cleaning — p.40
steps.warn: Keep the lubricant light. In cold weather heavy grease or oil can congeal and slow or stop the hammer fall.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Barrel off the stock, bore flushed and dry, nipple out and clean, lock wiped down. That is the full extent to which Thompson/Center disassembles this rifle. The reassembly sequence — which has one real trap in it — is in the Deep Clean.
steps.quote: NEVER DISASSEMBLE YOUR FIREARM beyond the procedures outlined in this manual.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Disassembly for Cleaning — p.39

deepSteps.title: Degrease anything the ignition touches
deepSteps.action: On a cap lock the fire channel behind the nipple must be clear and dry. Oil left in it after cleaning is the commonest cause of a cap that pops without lighting the charge.
deepSteps.quote: Remove any fouling on the exterior parts with an cloth dampened with T/C’s Number 13® Bore Cleaner - followed by drying and a light application of oil suitable for firearms.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Disassembly for Cleaning — p.40

deepSteps.title: Seat the hooked breech before the barrel goes down
deepSteps.action: This is the one step that goes wrong. The breech plug hook must be fully into the hole in the tang BEFORE you tip the barrel down into the channel. If the barrel resists coming together with the forend, that resistance is the hook not seated — stop and re-seat it rather than forcing it.
deepSteps.quote: Grasp the barrel, and insert the hooked breech into the hole in the tang, making sure that the breech plug fits closely against the tang before tipping the barrel down into the forearm channel.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Re-assembly of the T/C Hawken™ — p.41
deepSteps.warn: Heavy resistance when bringing the forend and barrel together means the hooked breech plug is not fully seated in the tang. Do not force it.

deepSteps.title: Refit the wedge pin
deepSteps.action: Hold the barrel and forend together and push the wedge pin through the escutcheon. It should be a snug fit and may need a gentle tap to fully engage.
deepSteps.quote: Hold the barrel and forearm of the stock together with your hand, and insert the wedge pin through the escutcheon hole in the forend.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual T/C Hawken™ Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:HAWKEN_103010, P/N 00016475 — Re-assembly of the T/C Hawken™ — p.41

cleaning.name: Bore
tasks: Solvent-soaked patches on the supplied jag until they come out clean
Muzzle in hot soapy water, pump a wet patch from the breech end to flush the barrel
Dry patches until the bore is completely dry
Light lubricant on the bore once dry

cleaning.name: Ignition
tasks: Unscrew the nipple and clean it and the threads in the barrel
Clear the fire channel behind the nipple
Dry the ignition parts thoroughly — leave no oil in the fire channel

cleaning.name: Lock and exterior
tasks: Wipe powder residue from the hammer/trigger assembly and receiver, then dry
Soft bristle brush with bore cleaner over the trigger guard assembly, then dry and lightly oil
Remove exterior fouling with a cloth dampened with bore cleaner, dry, then a light oil

reassembly: Refit the nipple into the drum
Insert the hooked breech into the hole in the tang and confirm the plug sits closely against the tang
Tip the barrel down into the barrel channel in the stock
Hold barrel and forend together and push the wedge pin through the escutcheon, tapping gently to fully engage
Return the ramrod to the thimbles
fncheck: With the rifle unprimed and uncharged, re-assemble and check for proper functioning of the hammer and trigger mechanism before loading and firing. Confirm the ramrod still protrudes about one inch from the muzzle, which shows the barrel is empty.
